title: cielociego: how often an optical satellite can actually see a field
description:
Measures, over a field's real polygon rather than over the whole 110 km tile, how often an optical satellite can actually see it, by reading the Sentinel-2 Scene Classification Layer inside the boundary instead of trusting the scene-level eo:cloud_cover metadata.

Measured over two fields in Magdalena, Colombia, across 2,794 days (2019-2026): Sentinel-2 acquired imagery on 599 and 601 of those days — the orbital revisit — and cloud measured inside the polygon made 47 % and 56 % of those acquisitions unusable. Combining both effects, no usable view existed on 89 % and 91 % of days; of that figure about 78.5 percentage points are the satellite's revisit and only 10 to 12 points are cloud, so the two contributions must be reported separately. The operationally relevant quantity is the waiting time, whose tail runs to 59 and 89 consecutive days with no usable view.

Uses Sentinel-2 L2A and Sentinel-1 GRD (Element84 STAC catalogue on AWS) and Sentinel-1 RTC (Microsoft Planetary Computer), with no account, no key and no cost. 219 offline tests, 84 % coverage, CI on Linux and Windows.
